description: MLQA is a multi-way aligned extractive QA evaluation benchmark designed to spur research in cross-lingual question answering. description: Largest publicly available multilingual context-grounded question-answering dataset for 11 major Indian languages from two language families. Encompasses both extractive and abstractive QA tasks incorporating existing datasets and English QA datasets translated into Indian languages. Synthetic dataset generated using Gemini model with manual verification. Combines Hindi SQuAD (5000 instances), XQuAD (1190 QA pairs), ChaII Dataset (1104 questions), IndicQA dataset (cloze-style reading comprehension), MLQA (4918 triples), MS MARCO (55k instances), NQ-Open, XORQA, LLaMA Index. Translate-Test paradigm significantly outperforms multilingual LLMs in low-resource languages. Evaluation using F1 scores for extractive QA and ROUGE-L for abstractive QA. Gemma2-Base performed best across most languages. BloomZ showed highest improvement for instruction-tuned models. Performance varies by resource availability: mid-resource languages (Hindi, Bengali) benefit from multilingual models while low-resource languages (Punjabi, Gujarati, Odia) perform better with translation-based approaches.
